subject: EU backup deletion & propagation questions — evidence & timing

Subject: EU backup deletion / propagation question

Hi Diego,

Quick question from our compliance team as we finalize the contract: under Redwood's current retention/deletion model, when a customer requests deletion of an EU tenant dataset, how soon do backups and replicated snapshots become irrecoverable? Our regulator requires demonstrable deletion within 30 days. In particular: 

- Do immutable snapshots or offsite replicas delay deletion beyond the tenant-requested day-zero delete?
- Are there cases where deletion is logical (tombstone) but objects remain physically present for >30 days?
- If a customer requests crypto-shred (KMS key destruction), is that available and how is it logged?

We need an evidence package (audit logs, snapshot purge records) to submit. If you can point to documentation or provide a short attestation for Acme Cloud’s EU tenancy, that would be ideal.

Thanks — Julie
Julie Ramos
Head of Platform Compliance
Acme Cloud

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Rishi (infra/serving) and Lauren (legal/compliance) to give a definitive, evidence-backed response. High-level notes below, and Rishi will follow up with specifics and logs we can provide. I also attached a retention matrix with our typical timelines (see acme-backup-retention-matrix.xlsx).

High-level:
- Primary deletion: when a tenant requests deletion, we mark objects for deletion (tombstone) and trigger snapshot retention enforcement immediately.
- Snapshot behavior: snapshots are immutable snapshots of block/object state; snapshot deletion is scheduled but may be subject to the snapshot garbage-collection window (normally 24–72 hours) depending on in-flight compactions and cross-region replication.
- Offsite/replicated copies: replication is asynchronous; we enforce deletion propagation but there can be a replication lag. For EU-only tenancy we prioritize intra-region operations; cross-region replication (if enabled) affects timing.
- Crypto-shred (KMS key destruction): available for Dedicated and Private deployments — key destruction is effectively irreversible; we log key destruction events in audit trails.

Propose a short call tomorrow to align on the evidence package and any contract language. Rishi / Lauren — can you confirm the maximum deletion propagation window we can attest to for EU-only accounts and list the logs we can export?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Lead — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: EU backup deletion / propagation question — infra details and evidence

Thanks Diego / Julie — below is a concise technical breakdown you can use in the attestation. I also attached our internal snapshot policy summary.

1) Snapshot and backup model (summary)- We create point-in-time snapshots of object stores and block volumes. Snapshots are reference-counted; deleting a snapshot decrements refcounts and triggers a garbage-collection (GC) pass.- GC scheduling: immediate in the control plane, physical reclamation typically occurs in scheduled GC waves; default window for physical expunge is 24–72 hours after GC trigger, but can extend to 7 days in cases of heavy compaction or live replication surges.

2) Replication and propagation- For EU-only tenants with replication disabled, deletes are local and complete within the GC window above.- If cross-region replication is enabled, deletion commands are propagated asynchronously and may take an additional replication delay (typically minutes to a few hours) plus the GC window on the replica side.

3) Tombstones vs physical deletion- Logical deletion (tombstone) is applied immediately and prevents application-level recovery; physical blocks/objects may persist until GC expunge. The combination of tombstone + GC expunge + replication confirmation is what we provide as evidence for 'irrecoverable' status.

4) Crypto-shred (KMS key destruction)- For customers requesting crypto-shred, we support KMS key destruction for Dedicated/Private setups. When keys are destroyed, data encrypted under those keys becomes cryptographically unrecoverable. Key destruction events are auditable (KMS event in Cloud KMS + Redwood audit log entry). Note: crypto-shred is irreversible and must be requested explicitly; it replaces standard object deletion as the strongest erasure assurance.

5) Legal-hold / litigation- If a legal hold is placed, deletion/GC is paused and we surface that as a compliance exception; we will not run GC on held objects until hold is released. We include hold reasons/ticket ids in the audit record.

6) Evidence we can provide- Deletion request record (control-plane event id)- Snapshot purge events (GC run ids and timestamps)- Replica-confirmation logs (if replication was enabled)- Audit log showing KMS key destruction (if used)

Recommended attestation wording we can provide for Acme Cloud: "For EU-only tenant X, Redwood enforces logical deletion at day-zero and will produce GC expunge logs and replica-confirmation events demonstrating physical reclamation within N days. For Dedicated/Private customers, crypto-shred (KMS destruction) is available upon request and is logged for audit."

Suggested max attestation window: we can confidently attest to a physical expunge within 7 days in worst-case scenarios for EU-only tenants without cross-region replication. If Acme requires a strict 30-day SLA, propose we set RPO/RTO and retention policy configuration to ensure 30-day irrecoverability in all edge cases and document it contractually.

Let me know if you want sample log extracts; we can export a redacted pack.

—Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Hi Julie — thanks for the patience. Per Rishi's notes above, summary and our proposed next steps to satisfy your regulator: 

Summary (plain language):
- We mark data for deletion immediately when you request it.
- Physical reclamation (expunge) is performed by GC; in normal conditions this completes within 24–72 hours; we allow for up to 7 days in rare heavy-replication/compaction cases.
- If cross-region replication is enabled, propagation adds additional delay; we recommend disabling cross-region replication for EU-residency-critical datasets.
- For the highest assurance, we offer crypto-shred (key destruction) for Dedicated or Private customers; this is irreversible and fully auditable.

Proposed actions for Acme Cloud:
1) We will configure your EU tenancy to disable cross-region replication for the datasets in scope.
2) We will set a documented retention/expunge policy contractually guaranteeing physical reclamation within 30 days and provide sample GC/purge log extracts after deletion tests.
3) If you require crypto-shred, we will document the KMS key-destruction process and schedule a destructive test with audit logs.

Next meeting: I proposed a 30-minute call for tomorrow 10:00–10:30 CEST to walk compliance through the evidence pack. If that works, I’ll send an invite and attach the redacted log packet afterwards.

When you have a moment, confirm the scope (tenant IDs or project names) and whether you want crypto-shred included in the standard workflow or only on explicit request.

Cheers,
Diego
